messages:
anna_support: FYI ACME reports a p99 spike on /v1/generate starting ~10:20 UTC. They say small requests (<=32 tokens) are hitting 2–8s occasionally. I attached a short trace and logs.

acme_ops: yes we've seen it on our side, started around 10:18. Most requests return 200 but tail is terrible. No deploys on our side.

drew_sre: looking at infra metrics — ingress waitlist depth jumped from ~20 to 400 on the small-req pool at 10:19. Tokens/sec steady, worker CPU not saturated. Possible admission control contention.

kai_runtime: can you paste the waitlist metrics? curious about per-worker concurrency and auth latencies.

anna_support: pasted: "waitlist_depth.small_requests: 380", "admit_rate.small_requests: 0.6/s", "inflight_per_worker: 24/32", "avg_auth_ms: 84", "auth_5xx_rate: 0.02%"

drew_sre: hmm auth latency is a little higher but not enough to explain this. I see a pattern of short-lived auth refresh calls every request for this tenant — looks like token refresh storm causing serialization on per-tenant lock in auth-proxy.

kai_runtime: that matches an earlier bug — when token cache misses, we serialise refreshes with a per-tenant mutex which can queue requests. If a tenant's refreshes start missing, many small requests pile up behind the lock. We had a rollback for that but maybe the canary didn't cover small reqs.

jasmine_csm: ACME is on Dedicated, peak traffic for them is low but bursty. They said they rotated keys yesterday afternoon.

drew_sre: possible root cause: key rotation + token cache TTL mismatch => cache miss storm => per-tenant mutex -> waitlist growth -> p99 regressions.

kai_runtime: mitigation options (short list):
- hotfix: make token refresh lock async (allow one refresher, early-fail others with 429 + retry-after) or use singleflight to de-dup but avoid serial blocking.
- temporary mitigation: bump small_request_pool size by 2x and increase admission burst for this tenant.
- customer workaround: ask ACME to avoid immediate heavy fanout during key rotation (not ideal).

anna_support: ACME wants a quick mitigation — can we do the temporary pool bump + per-tenant admit bump? what's the risk?

drew_sre: pool bump is low-risk, might increase GPU memory usage but CPU/IO is fine. Per-tenant admit bump is safe for short window; watch fallback capacity. I'll run the change on prod-slot-3.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by drew_sre: increase small_request_pool=64 -> 128 on prod-slot-3. Rollout 1/3.

drew_sre: rollout step 1 successful, waitlist depth halved on slot-3 within 30s. Still seeing some tail on other slots.

kai_runtime: pushing a runtime patch to make auth refresh singleflight non-blocking in parallel, I'll open a canary and link PR.

kai_runtime: PR #5789: non-blocking singleflight for token refresh — canary deployment to slot-3 ready.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of runtime PR #5789 to prod-slot-3 complete.

drew_sre: after both mitigations on slot-3 p99 for ACME dropped from 2.8s -> 320ms. Rolling the pool bump to other slots now.

anna_support: ACME confirms improved tail on their end, thank you. They asked for root-cause doc and we should schedule a postmortem if PR changes are needed.

jasmine_csm: I'll coordinate a customer note and recommended key-rotation checklist so they don't cause a refresh storm next time.

kai_runtime: I'll follow-up with a small postmortem PR and recommend we add synthetic tests for token-cache-miss scenarios to prevent regressions.

acme_ops: thanks team — appreciate the quick response. We'll defer any more rotations until you confirm the fix is rolled everywhere.

anna_support: last step — monitor waitlist and token-refresh-miss metrics for 24h, will create watch alert if queue depth > 100 for any slot. :eyes:
